text:
Maya: Tiny culture question: what's the strangest 'house' or 'flat' rule you've ever followed? mine: everyone freezes if a plant is being watered. silent ceremony. :seedling:

Jamal: My old flat had a sock drawer rota. every Sunday you had to fold socks like origami. missed a week = you did dishes for two days. :socks:

Sofia: We had a 'microwave curator' - only one person could press start for communal lunches because someone kept nuking everyone's food for 90s. curatorship was serious. :sparkles:

Elliot: 'No hot drinks on the couch' - agreed after a betrayal that left a permanent latte stain. couch still judgey. :couch_and_lamp:

Maya: @Jamal origami socks sounds delightfully specific. did anyone learn to fold a swan?

Jamal: @Maya one swan, many tears. it was mostly triangles.

Sofia: Small honor code we had: if you borrow a hoodie, you return it with the pocket lint removed. gross but fair. :shower:

kudos-bot: :tada: Shoutout to @Sofia for organizing the mystery bookshelf swap last month! :books:

Elliot: Also saw a sign once: 'Please do not feed the roommate after midnight.' still not sure if it was about snacks or karaoke.

Maya: Okay last quick poll - which of these tiny rules would you adopt for a new flat? 1) Silent plant-watering ceremony 2) Microwave curator 3) Sock folding rota 4) No hot drinks on couch. reply with the number.

Jamal: 3

Sofia: 2

Elliot: 4

Maya: 1 (for the vibes)

kudos-bot: Reminder: community fridge rule reminder 63 unlabeled food older than 4 days will be cleared on Friday. :framed_picture:

Sofia: This thread is gold. saving ideas for my future dubious cohabitation. :laughing:
